answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a shared vault before it may submit bids, with rewards released only after a randomly selected peer verifies the work. Because one operator must fund every identity separately, splitting into a swarm does not multiply influence for free: the attacker ties up capital and risks losing each bond when a claim fails. A ferrous key or onyx badge alone proves nothing; the costly, slashable deposit does the work.
